summary: Designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, this interactive web application transforms complex space science into an engaging visual experience. Users begin their journey inside **The Chamber**, an atmospheric and interactive gateway designed to bridge visitors directly into deep-space exploration. From there, they can navigate a live **3D Solar System** observatory complete with dynamic planetary orbits, realistic lighting, and responsive controls. To deepen scientific discovery, the platform also integrates a **Location Comparer**, allowing users to conduct side-by-side geological and environmental evaluations between terrestrial field sites on Earth and analogue regions across Mars and the Moon. Built on a unified React and Three.js architecture, the project brings together modular exploration tools, research compendiums, and fluid 60fps performance across desktop and mobile devices.
details: EarthExplore is an innovative project developed by **Team GAVA**, consisting of four members, for the NASA Space Apps Hackathon. Our project focuses on identifying Earth locations that have environmental, geographical, and geological similarities to potential permanent Moon-base locations and Mars environments. The main idea is to help researchers, scientists, students, and space enthusiasts understand how different places on Earth can be used to study conditions similar to those found on other planets. Through EarthExplore, users can select the Moon or Mars, explore their environmental characteristics, compare them with information about different locations on Earth, and discover possible Earth analog sites. For example, the Atacama Desert in Chile provides an opportunity to study extremely dry and barren environments, Antarctica offers conditions for studying extreme cold and isolation, and volcanic regions such as Iceland and Hawaii provide geological features that can be compared with planetary landscapes. The platform aims to use relevant NASA open planetary data and Earth observation information to support these comparisons, depending on the datasets actually integrated into the prototype. Important comparison factors may include temperature, terrain, geology, elevation, dryness, and environmental conditions. EarthExplore is designed to make planetary research more accessible, improve space science education, and help researchers identify suitable Earth-based environments for field studies and astronaut preparation. However, Earth locations cannot perfectly reproduce the Moon's or Mars's conditions, such as low gravity, radiation, vacuum, or different atmospheric conditions; they can only provide useful comparisons for selected environmental features. In the future, EarthExplore could be improved with AI-based recommendations, similarity scores, 3D terrain visualisation, satellite imagery, and additional environmental datasets. Our vision is to make EarthExplore a useful platform for discovering the connections between our planet and other worlds, because understanding Earth is an important step towards exploring beyond Earth
